key_insight: CoCo-Prover turns theorem proving into a cost-aware orchestration problem, using proof-graph structure to decide both which goals to tackle and which specialist agent calls to buy.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for large-scale program verification because it aims to maximize verified obligations per dollar, not just raw proof success.
method: Builds a two-level proof representation: an intra-declaration AND/OR proof hypergraph plus an inter-declaration lemma-dependency graph.
Selects open goals symbolically via topological traversal of the proof graphs.
Uses an agentic router to allocate bounded, priced specialist invocations with evolving routing rules as evidence accumulates.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on five Lean 4 verification benchmarks (CLEVER, VERINA, AlgoVeri, NTP4VC, and Vero), where it achieved the best solve rate on every benchmark, up to 100% on two, and cut cost by up to 30.9% versus the strongest baseline.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate proof-graph modeling and effective routing policies, so performance may be sensitive to benchmark structure and specialist-agent configuration.
paper_title: Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving via Agent Orchestration in Program Verification
